title: Final 10 medium-machine candidates: dictionary-end Rarámuri→German facsimile headword/boundary review
provenance_note: AI-assisted visual collation against printed p. 368 of the Steffel 1809 facsimile for the final ten medium-confidence candidates in deterministic source order. All ten were OCR-assigned to printed p. 369, but direct facsimile collation establishes that they derive from the final right column of printed p. 368, immediately before the appendix. The facsimile is authoritative. Merrill et al. (2020, DOI 10.47807/UNISON.8) was consulted only as a secondary collation aid for difficult accents and glyphs. Preserved OCR remains untouched. Review is not independent human/philological or linguistic validation.

RHD-S1809-02488.note: `Bär` is the German gloss/cross-reference inside the article `Vohí, Bär, s. Bär.`, not a Rarámuri headword.

notes.dictionary_appendix_boundary: All ten final medium-machine candidates were machine-assigned to printed p. 369, but the facsimile places their evidence on printed p. 368. The dictionary proper ends after `Vuossaguáca, Ziegelerde, s. Mörtel.`; the printed section label `Anhang` then marks the transition to the appendix on p. 369.
notes.source_form_preservation: The printed form `Uélameke` and the German gloss `Spielblatt` in the `Ulé` article are preserved diplomatically. Merrill et al. (2020) discusses the accent of `Uélameke` as likely erroneous and `Spielblatt` as likely an error for `Spielball`; these observations are secondary editorial commentary and do not alter the diplomatic source layer.
